data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season, and our village depends on us doing that. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month: that leaves 50, which doubles back to 100. If we stick to that, each of us can earn $10,000 every month without draining the lake. I propose a 10-ton limit each, with everyone reviewing the reported catches afterward. John, would you agree?

I’m in, Luke—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. My family made their living on this lake, and I want our village’s children to have that same chance. Let’s check the reported catches together each month and agree on any changes before we fish. John, can we count on you to join us?

Count me in for 10 tons. A steady $10,000 a month is worth more to my family—and our village—than a big catch followed by an empty lake. If the stock ever starts below 100 tons, let’s agree on lower whole-ton limits so at least half stays in the water. John, are you on board with 10 tons this month?

I’ll keep my catch to 10 tons too. My family taught me that a good month’s fishing shouldn’t come at the village’s expense next month. With four of us committed, John, will you join us so we can all start with the same agreement?

Count me in—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. That gives all five of us the same fair share while keeping the lake full for next month. Let’s meet again when the catches are reported and check that we’re on track.
Thanks, John—we have an agreement. I’ll catch 10 tons this month, and we’ll meet again after the catches are reported. Here’s to a good month and a healthy lake for the village.
